dct_title_s: Fires and Thermal Anomalies (Night), Terra and Aqua / MODIS
dct_description_sm: The Aqua and Terra MODIS Fire and Thermal Anomalies layer shows active fire detections and thermal anomalies, such as volcanoes, and gas flares. Fires can be set naturally, such as by lightning, or by humans, whether intentionally or accidentally. Fire is often thought of as a menace and detriment to life, but in some ecosystems it is necessary to maintain the equilibrium, for example, some plants only release seeds under high temperatures that can only be achieved by fire, fires can also clear undergrowth and brush to help restore forests to good health, humans use fire in slash and burn agriculture, to clear away last year’s crop stubble and provide nutrients for the soil and to clear areas for pasture. The fire layer is useful for studying the spatial and temporal distribution of fire, to locate persistent hot spots such as volcanoes and gas flares, to locate the source of air pollution from smoke that may have adverse human health impacts.

The MODIS Fire and Thermal Anomalies product is available from the Terra (MOD14) and Aqua (MYD14) satellites as well as a combined Terra and Aqua (MCD14) satellite product. The sensor resolution is 1 km, and the temporal resolution is daily. The thermal anomalies are represented as points (approximate center of a 1 km pixel) in Worldview/GIBS.

A daily visualization from NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), available from 2002-07-04 and updated as new data arrive. Made from MODIS/Aqua Terra Thermal Anomalies/Fire locations 1km FIRMS NRT (Vector data) (MCD14DL, version 6.1NRT, doi:10.5067/FIRMS/MODIS/MCD14DL.NRT.0061).
